coverage_exempt.reason: Original allocation-failure continuation cannot return here: 0x4db6e0 sets EBP to the null realloc result, then 0x4dc680 reads [EBP+4] and faults at address 4. Reproduced by original source dispatch allocation-failure probe in work/level-seven-bear-cases-5.log.

The original rechecks the identical state index and table bounds after resolving its slot, with no intervening outside call or change to the bounds. A successful first growth includes the requested index. This second growth arm therefore cannot execute; the first failure arm faults before returning.

The second lookup failure continuation requires the unreachable second growth arm to return zero. The original realloc-failure path instead sets EBP to zero and faults on [EBP+4] at 0x4dc680, reproduced in work/level-seven-bear-cases-5.log.

equivalent_mutants.reason: Original store 0x40a0ae is in the first table-allocation failure continuation. The unchanged 0x4db6e0 sets EBP to the null realloc result at 0x4db70b or 0x4db77f, then calls 0x4dc680, which reads address 4 and faults before returning zero. The original fault is reproduced in work/level-seven-bear-cases-5.log. Removing this unreachable store cannot affect any returning permitted input.

Original store 0x40a128 is in the second table-allocation failure continuation. Original 0x40a082 through 0x40a0dc performs no outside call or bounds write between successful first lookup and identical second bounds check, so the second growth arm cannot execute. In addition, a failed 0x4db6e0 realloc faults at 0x4dc680 before returning zero, as reproduced in work/level-seven-bear-cases-5.log. Removing this unreachable store cannot affect any permitted input.
